survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a conceptual framework and does not conduct an empirical large-scale assessment analysis with student microdata. It therefore does not specify sampling frames, complex survey design features, or the application of ILSA/PISA-style student weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife). Because no achievement scores are estimated from plausible values (PV-based scaling) and no analytic sample is modeled, there is no weight variable to apply for inference. For any future empirical implementation of the proposed metrics, analysts should use the official ILSA/PISA weight variables and PV procedures provided by the relevant assessment data products.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The paper is not an empirical ML study using ILSA/PISA microdata; it proposes a conceptual architecture and pedagogical/system implications for education for human flourishing. As a result, plausible values (PV-based achievement scaling) are not generated or analyzed, and there is no missing-data handling procedure to report for an estimation model. Any missing-data considerations would only arise in a future operationalisation where student-level assessment items/scores are analysed quantitatively.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No student-level dataset is analysed. The chapter provides conceptual and policy/pedagogical guidance (including examples from Singapore’s NIE and other initiatives) rather than an empirical study with an analytic sample.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD chapter develops a conceptual framework for “Education for human flourishing,” focusing on five learner competencies (adaptive problem-solving, ethical competence, understanding the world, appreciating the world, acting in the world) and a broader architecture linking them to foundational literacies, social-emotional skills, and well-being domains. It also proposes learning-environment design principles (curricular, pedagogical, aesthetic, social-emotional, exploratory-imaginative, digital, and physical spaces) and pedagogical features (teacher-guided learning and experiential learning), with illustrative technology-enabled examples (e.g., TEL tools and the Knowledge Building Design Studio). The document does not estimate statistical models, train ML predictors, or report performance metrics against an assessment outcome. Consequently, there are no benchmarks, effect sizes, or causal claims to evaluate; the contribution is normative and design-oriented, intended to inform future metric selection and assessment development rather than to test an empirical hypothesis.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse because the document is a conceptual framework and policy/pedagogical guidance rather than an empirical large-scale assessment or ML study. It does not report an analytic sample, country-level student counts, PV handling, missing-data procedures, or any predictive modeling results. Therefore, fields related to empirical ML methods and findings are intentionally left empty.
